title: Murder at Blackwood Manor
tagline: A dark and stormy night. A locked library. Four suspects, and every one of them is hiding something.
intro:
Thunder rattles the windows of Blackwood Manor. The lights have gone out, the road has flooded, and nobody is going anywhere tonight.

Somewhere between the port and the coffee, Lord Blackwood was found dead in his own locked library, and the key is nowhere to be found.

The butler is polishing things that are already clean. The lady of the house keeps fainting. The business partner is shouting. The gardener won't look anyone in the eye. Grab your magnifying glass, detective: someone in this house is a murderer.

victim.name: Lord Blackwood
victim.description: Master of Blackwood Manor: rich, sharp-tongued and famously hard to please. Everyone in the house owed him something, and he never let them forget it.
victim.causeOfDeath: A single heavy blow to the head. His monocle is still in shock.

locations.name: The Library
locations.description: Lord Blackwood's book-lined sanctum at the end of the hall. One oak door to the hall with a single key; tall windows shuttered and bolted against the storm; a coal fire.

lines: A dying fire, a splintered door and four thousand books that saw everything and aren't saying a word.
You tiptoe around his lordship's favourite rug. Somewhere, a violin plays one very ominous note.
searchFlavor.emptyLine: You re-check the shelves, the rug and the dead fire. Four thousand books, still not talking. Nothing new here.

locations.name: The Dining Room
locations.description: Long table, a pair of silver candlesticks and a roaring hearth.

lines: Dinner for four, abandoned mid-pudding. A lone silver candlestick stands on the table, looking for its other half.
The fire has sulked down to embers, and the hearth wears the smug look of a fireplace that knows something.
searchFlavor.emptyLine: You count the pudding bowls again. Still four. Still nobody finished the trifle. Nothing new here.

locations.lockedLine: Crime scene first, detective! Procedure! Start where his lordship fell, and the dining room will still be here when you get back.

locations.name: The Hall
locations.description: The manor's central hall joining every room. Tall windows, a grandfather clock, and a garden door with a dark alcove beside it.

lines: The grandfather clock ticks, the thunder booms, and every portrait on the wall seems to be staring at the library door.
Doors in every direction, a draughty garden door that won't stop rattling, and puddles. Mind the puddles.
searchFlavor.emptyLine: You stare at the portraits. The portraits stare back. The grandfather clock clears its throat. Nothing new here.

locations.name: The Garden
locations.description: Lawns, greenhouse and potting shed, lashed by the storm. The garden door leads into the hall; the kitchen door leads into the servants' quarters.

lines: Rain, mud, a sulking greenhouse and one extremely soggy scarecrow. The storm has rinsed away everything but the worms.
Beside the garden door lies a storm lantern, snuffed out and abandoned. Somebody came in out of the dark in a hurry, and left their light behind.
searchFlavor.emptyLine: You search the flowerbeds again and find mud, more mud, and a snail who refuses to answer questions. The lantern has told you all it is going to.

locations.name: Kitchen & Servants' Quarters
locations.description: Kitchen, the butler's pantry, and the manor's only telephone on the wall of the servants' passage.

lines: Copper pans gleam, a kettle grumbles on the range, and the whole place smells of boiled cabbage and nerves.
The servants' telephone hangs a little crooked on its hook, with a soggy shred of cigar stuck to the mouthpiece. Somebody has been chewing on their calls.
searchFlavor.emptyLine: You check the bread bin, the biscuit tin and behind the mangle. Plenty of crumbs, nothing else to find.

facts.statement: The library door has a single key and there is no spare.
Lord Blackwood always locked himself in the library when he worked, leaving the key in the lock on the inside, and unlocked it only to admit someone.
Throughout the storm the library windows were shuttered and bolted from inside, so the hall door was the only way in or out.
The silver candlestick found in the library is one of a matching pair that belongs on the dining table.
The fresh candle Reginald fitted into the silver candlestick at 21:12 burned for only about five minutes before it fell over and went out.
Lord Blackwood had his solicitor draw up a new will that cut Victoria down to two hundred pounds a year. He was to sign it at ten o'clock the next morning.
Under the existing will Victoria inherits nearly everything, so Lord Blackwood's death before the new will was signed would leave her the fortune.
The solicitor's letter also says the household accounts point to the butler and advises an audit.
Archibald Crane had been embezzling money from his and Lord Blackwood's company, and Lord Blackwood had found out.
Reginald has been skimming money from the household accounts for years and keeps the cash hidden in his pantry.
Lord Blackwood dismissed Gregory that morning for drinking on duty.
The muddy hobnail boot print in the hall alcove by the garden door was made by Gregory's boots.
No mud was tracked beyond the garden-door alcove; the rest of the hall and the library carpet are free of mud.

After hearing the library lock turn at 21:13, Reginald went below stairs and stayed in his pantry until he carried the coal up at 21:30. In all that time he saw no one in the hall or at the library door, and he did not see Victoria at all.
At 21:32, when the library door gave way, Reginald saw that the solicitor's letter, which had lain open on the desk at 21:12, was no longer there.

motives.label: Inheritance
motives.description: Someone stood to gain from Lord Blackwood's fortune, but only if he died at the right moment.

motives.label: Business ruin
motives.description: Someone faced disgrace, or prison, if Lord Blackwood talked.

motives.label: Stolen money
motives.description: Someone had been quietly helping themselves, and his lordship was getting close.

motives.label: Revenge
motives.description: Someone had a score to settle with his lordship.

leads.title: What struck his lordship down?
leads.hint: Somebody used something heavy. The library is where it happened, so that is where a tidy detective starts.
leads.closedLine: A candlestick! The butler will be mortified about the polish.

leads.title: Who gains from his death?
leads.hint: Money, grudges and who-gets-what: somebody in this house is better off tonight. Find out what they were fighting over.
leads.closedLine: Paper never lies, though it does burn.

leads.title: Where does a key go when it leaves a locked room?
leads.hint: The library door was locked and the key was gone. Keys do not walk. Somebody carried it out, so where would they put it?
leads.closedLine: The key, found. It had been sulking in the coal.

leads.title: Her ladyship keeps eyeing the dining-room fireplace
leads.hint: Lady Victoria's gaze drifts to the dining-room hearth whenever you press her. Fires keep their own counsel, but not for ever.
leads.closedLine: Her ladyship's favourite fireplace gave up its first secret.

leads.title: A letter on the desk at 21:12, gone by 21:32
leads.hint: Reginald saw a letter lying open on his lordship's desk at 21:12. By 21:32 the desk was bare. Papers do not walk off either.
leads.closedLine: The letter, rescued from the flames and only slightly toasted.

leads.title: A snuffed lantern by the garden door
leads.hint: A storm lantern lies snuffed out beside the garden door. Who came in out of the dark? The hall by that door may remember.
leads.closedLine: The lantern's owner left a footprint behind. People never think of the floor.

leads.title: The gardener never looks up from his boots
leads.hint: Gregory will not lift his eyes from his boots. Boots go places, and floors remember them. The hall is where boots get noticed.
leads.closedLine: The boots had been in the hall after all.

leads.title: Who was really with whom during the blackout?
leads.hint: Two people swear they were together every minute. Somebody's story is going to spring a leak. Find whose, and make them say so.
leads.closedLine: One story has a hole in it, and now everybody can see through.

leads.title: Did anyone see who stood at the library door?
leads.hint: The hall has a clear view of the library door. If somebody was lurking about in the dark, they may have seen more than they let on.
leads.closedLine: A witness, at last, and a lightning flash to thank for it.

lockedLines.evidence: A hunch and a hat don't close a case, detective. Keep looking.
lockedLines.suspects: You've barely spoken to the household! Everyone has something to say, and somebody is fibbing.
lockedLines.secrets: Plenty of chatter, no cracks. Somebody here is sitting on a story. Lean on them with what's in your notebook.
lockedLines.leads: One of tonight's stories hasn't been put to the test yet. Somebody is still telling it with a straight face.
lockedLines.default: Not so fast, detective! The case isn't ready for the gavel.
